content.title: Fannie, Freddie privatization back in focus but major changes likely gradual: BofA
content.summary: Investing.com-- Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac privatization is back in focus as U.S. regulators signal possible steps to end conservatorships. But Bank of America expects any major change to be gradual, with government backing remaining firmly in place for now.

content.title: Bill Ackman’s Main Fund Is Up 25% in 2025. These 2 Investments Are Helping.
content.summary: Bill Ackman is having an impressive year: His main investment vehicle has returned 25% and been helped by its sizable holdings in  Freddie Mac  and Fannie Mae, whose shares have more than quadrupled in 2025.  The fund’s U.S.-listed shares closed 1% higher on Friday at $63.41 apiece after hitting a record high of $63.70 earlier in the session.  The shares have returned 32% so far this year, topping the NAV performance as the discount to NAV has narrowed.

content.title: Fannie, Freddie Get First Bull on Wall Street in Deutsche Bank
content.summary: Fannie Mae shares have jumped more than 320% year-to-date and Freddie Mac shares have surged 288% for the same period.  While both were delisted from the New York Stock Exchange in 2010, their shares are bought and sold over the counter, where trading is often volatile.

content.title: Fannie, Freddie Execs Led Government Meeting About Regulating Their Business
content.summary: A government regulatory meeting this week focused on reforms to mortgage giants Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac was led at least in part by executives from those companies.  The Trump administration and Federal Housing Finance Agency Director Bill Pulte have embarked on an effort to resolve the fates of giants Fannie and Freddie, which backstop nearly $7 trillion in mortgage-backed securities and provide the backbone for the U.S. housing market.  Pulte’s FHFA, which regulates Fannie and Freddie, held its first major housing-finance reform meeting this week.
